# Closest-results comparison

- Classical compact-manifold heat-kernel theory gives local asymptotics,
  Gaussian estimates, and cut-locus structure.  Chen--Li--Wu (2023) and
  Neel--Sacchelli (2025) give substantially more general logarithmic and
  cut-locus asymptotics; the present paper specializes to SU(2) and supplies
  computable finite-time derivative constants.
- Compact-group theory supplies the spectral expansion and convolution law.
  The present contribution is the formula-adaptive, full-class-angle
  enclosure with explicit positivity conditions.
- Menotti--Onofri and Manton provide the lattice heat-kernel and geodesic
  actions.  Bitar--Duke--Jadid treat renormalization questions.  None of
  these sources supplies the arbitrary finite-order rational bounds derived
  here.
- Kanwar--Wagman illustrates current interest in exact heat-kernel transfer
  matrices.  It motivates numerical reliability but is not a theorem
  dependency.

The defensible contribution is the combination of a global SU(2) atlas,
arbitrary finite derivative order, explicit cut-chart lower bounds, and a
reproducible rational specialization.  No priority, optimality, interacting
measure, or mass-gap claim is made.
